Our reliance on fossil fuel combustion is ruining carbon dating

Carbon dating has never been accurate and never will be. The reason is that in order to get a proper measurement, you must assume something about the past that isn't known and can't be proven - the ratio of radioactive carbon to normal carbon. We have a reference for how much radioactive carbon we would expect to find in Earth's environment right now, but we have zero historical data on how that number has changed.

A local volcanic eruption could easily disrupt the balance of radioctive to non-radioactive carbon in an area for a good many years. Changes in the upper atmosphere could result in a very different ratio being produced. A meteor impact could do the same thing. Changes in solar activity. Even the presence of organisms that may prefer one form of carbon to another would screw things up.
Great point! We can only adjust measurements for events that we know of, and the farther back you go the more likely there is an unknown event we're not adjusting for.
